decisions.reason: The 1500 RPM maximum changes the drive constraint but does not alter the candidate's mixing-quality or foam outcomes; the same message's separate whisk selection is already represented.
The motor-speed maximum does not change the selected bowl capacity, depth, enclosure constraint, or refilling policy.
The motor-speed maximum does not change the requirement that bowls be quickly removable and swappable.
Although motor speed may influence splashing during operation, the source does not change the existing splash target or conditional splash-guard policy.
A same-message MODIFY already completely records that the motor and related control components must support a maximum operating speed of 1500 RPM.
The motor-speed maximum does not change the dispensing mechanism, sequence, flow constraints, or texture-preservation requirement.
Selecting a 1500 RPM maximum does not change the requirement to use simple off-the-shelf electrical components for the first prototype.
The speed limit does not change the existing stability behavior or specified stabilization features; any redesign for vibration would require additional evidence.
The source does not change the CAD deliverable or system-layout requirement, and no necessary layout alteration is specified.
The source does not modify the requirement to provide a basic wiring plan or specify a new wiring-plan attribute.
